title: How Iman Gadzhi went from dropout to $2M with an SMMA: outreach, retainers, systems
summary: Iman recounts building a social media agency from a £300/month soccer club client to six figures a month. He covers the fake audit cold outreach, the Expedia-style contractor model, why results-based services beat content retainers, and the founder discipline that kept him scaling.

principles.text: Cold outreach: use a fake video audit with a play button so replies show who is ready.
principles.quote: I just take a photo of their home screen add a little play button so it looks like it's a video even though it's on the email

principles.text: Pitch business owners on 'leaving money on the table' and a mismatch between their brand and their size.
principles.quote: your social media isn't congruent to the size of your business

principles.text: Sell services and hire contractors to deliver, so you're a business owner, not a glorified contractor.
principles.quote: I realize I am the headless chicken you know I'm client I'm delivering these services for my clients I'm doing it myself I'm not a business owner

principles.text: Work on the business, not in it: build systems, test them, then move to the next one.
principles.quote: you need to work on the business not in it

principles.text: Hire passionate contractors from niche communities like Facebook groups, not gig marketplaces.
principles.quote: the best place to look is actually Facebook groups

principles.text: Use a three-month minimum contract so day-30 emotional decisions don't kill the client.
principles.quote: just making sure that you do a three month minimum for all of your agency clients just allows you that breathing room
